summary: This note is a list of the sixteen counties in the U.S. state of Maine, with historical context. Maine was part of Massachusetts as the District of Maine before becoming a state on March 15, 1820, as part of the Missouri Compromise. Nine counties were defined before statehood, and the northern border dispute with Britain was not settled until the Webster-Ashburton Treaty of 1842, which also affected most of Aroostook County.
one_line: A list of Maine's sixteen counties, with their pre-statehood origins and the northern border dispute settled by the 1842 Webster-Ashburton Treaty.
key_facts: Maine has sixteen counties, and this note is a list of them.
Before statehood, Maine was officially part of the state of Massachusetts and was called the District of Maine.
Maine was granted statehood on March 15, 1820, as part of the Missouri Compromise.
Nine of the sixteen counties had their borders defined while Maine was still part of Massachusetts.
The nine counties whose borders were defined before statehood are older than the state itself.
After 1820, the exact location of Maine's northern border was disputed with Britain.
The northern border dispute with Britain was settled by the Webster-Ashburton Treaty, signed in 1842.
The northern counties reached their final official form with the Webster-Ashburton Treaty.
Almost all of Aroostook County was disputed land until the Webster-Ashburton Treaty was signed.
